4.84.m: Skanda said:
Listen, O brahmin (kṣoṇīsura), how Sthāṇu (Śiva) created
The sacred ground of fords from the holy confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Varaṇā. // 1

4.84.s: saṃgame tatra niṣṇātaḥ saṃgameśaṃ samarcya ca ..
4.84.d: संगमे तत्र निष्णातः संगमेशं समर्च्य च ..
4.84.m: Having bathed at that confluence and worshipped Saṃgameśa,
A man shall never again enter the womb of a mother. // 2

4.84.s: tatra pādodakaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra devena śārṅgiṇā ..
4.84.d: तत्र पादोदकं तीर्थं यत्र देवेन शार्ङ्गिणा ..
4.84.m: There is the sacred ford Pādodaka, where by the bow-wielding God (Śārṅgin/Viṣṇu)...

4.84.s: ādau pādau kṣalitau tu maṃdarāccāgatena yat .. 3 ..
4.84.d: आदौ पादौ क्षलितौ तु मंदराच्चागतेन यत् .. 3 ..
4.84.m: where the bow-wielding god washed his feet first when he came from Mandara.
Whoever performs the water-rite at the sacred ford of Viṣṇu's foot-water,
his course in saṃsāra is certainly overturned through this change.
Having performed his ritual ablution at Pādodaka and worshipped Keśava,
the best of men has ended his dwelling in saṃsāra and remains in Kāśī.

4.84.s: kāśyāṃ sā bhūmiruddiṣṭā śvetadvīpa iti dvijaiḥ ..
4.84.d: काश्यां सा भूमिरुद्दिष्टा श्वेतद्वीप इति द्विजैः ..
4.84.m: That ground in Kāśī is declared by the twice-born to be Śvetadvīpa;
having earned merit there, one becomes the lord of Śvetadvīpa.
Beyond that sacred ford of Pādodaka is the sacred ford named Kṣīrābdhi;
having earned great merit there, one dwells on the shore of the Ocean of Milk.
South of Kṣīroda is the unsurpassed sacred ford called Śaṅkha;
having bathed there, a man surely becomes master of the Śaṅkha and other treasures.
And on this side of Śaṅkhatīrtha is the unsurpassed Cakratīrtha;
by plunging into the water of that sacred ford, one does not fall into the wheel of saṃsāra.
In front of it is Gadātīrtha, which destroys the disease of saṃsāra;
by performing the śrāddha and other rites there, one beholds the mace-bearing god Gadādhara.
And in front of it is Padmatīrtha, shaped like a lotus, which brings satisfaction to the ancestors;
by performing ritual ablutions and other rites there, one attains the destruction of sins.
Then there is the sacred ford of Mahālakṣmī, which grants the fruit of great merit;
having worshipped Mahālakṣmī there, one obtains the lotus of nirvāṇa.
Then there is Gārutmatatīrtha, which destroys the poison of saṃsāra;
having performed the water-rites there, one attains an abode in Vaikuṇṭha.
Then there is Nāradatīrtha, the sole cause of the knowledge of Brahman;
by bathing there and beholding Nāradakeśava, one becomes liberated.
South of it is Prahlādatīrtha, which grants the fruit of great devotion;

4.84.s: tatra vai snānamātreṇa viṣṇoḥ priyataro bhavet .. 15 ..
4.84.d: तत्र वै स्नानमात्रेण विष्णोः प्रियतरो भवेत् .. 15 ..
4.84.m: by merely bathing there, one becomes most dear to Viṣṇu.
Then there is the sacred ford Aṃbarīṣa, which destroys great sins;

4.84.s: tatra vai śubhakarmāṇo janā no garbhabhājanam .. .. 16 ..
4.84.d: तत्र वै शुभकर्माणो जना नो गर्भभाजनम् .. .. 16 ..
4.84.m: people of auspicious deeds who go there never become receptacles of a womb.
In front of it is the excellent sacred ford named Ādityakeśava;
having performed consecration there, one obtains consecration in heaven.
There is the sacred ford of Dattātreya, which purifies the three worlds;
by merely bathing there with faith, one attains perfection in yoga.
In front of it is Bhārgavatīrtha, which bestows supreme knowledge;
by the rule of ritual ablution there, one comes to share the world of Bhārgava.
Then there is Vāmanatīrtha, which causes Viṣṇu's presence;
by the performance of a śrāddha there, one is freed from the debt born of the ancestors.
Then there is the auspicious sacred ford named Naranārāyaṇa;
by plunging into that sacred ford, dwelling in a womb is very hard for men to obtain.
And south of it is the auspicious Yajñavārāhatīrtha,

4.84.s: yatra snātasya vai puṃsāṃ rājasūyaphalaṃ dhruvam.. 22 ..
4.84.d: यत्र स्नातस्य वै पुंसां राजसूयफलं ध्रुवम्.. 22 ..
4.84.m: bathing where men certainly obtain the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice.
There is the purifying sacred ford named Vidāranārasiṃha;
where by a single ritual ablution sin earned over a hundred births is destroyed.
And beyond that is Gopīgovindatīrtha, which grants the world of Viṣṇu;
a wise man who has bathed in it does not experience the pain of the womb.
And south of Gopīgovinda is Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhatīrtha;
the best of men who resides there is chosen by the Lakṣmī of nirvāṇa.
In the southern quarter from it is the unsurpassed Śeṣatīrtha;
by plunging into which even the remainder of a mass of great sins does not remain.
And in the southern direction is the excellent Śaṅkhamādhavatīrtha;
from serving that sacred ford, whence could men have any great fear of sin?
Even more purifying than that is the sacred ford that gives immediate accomplishment;
it is the peerless Nīlagrīvatīrtha; one who bathes in it is ever pure.
There is Uddālakatīrtha, which destroys the mass of all sins;
by merely bathing there, it grants great prosperity to men.

4.84.s: tataḥ sāṃkhyākhya tīrthaṃ ca sāṃkhyeśvara samīpataḥ ..
4.84.d: ततः सांख्याख्य तीर्थं च सांख्येश्वर समीपतः ..
4.84.m: Then there is the sacred ford named Sāṅkhya near Sāṅkhyeśvara;
by serving that sacred ford, the yoga of Sāṅkhya becomes clear to men.
Where the god Umā's lord himself merged [after coming] from heaven,
there is therefore Svarlīnatīrtha, in the presence of Svarlīneśvara.
By ritual ablution, giving gifts, feeding the twice-born with faith,
by recitation of mantras, oblations, and worship there, everything indeed becomes imperishable for men.
And near it is the extremely purifying Mahiṣāsuratīrtha.

4.84.s: yatra taptvā sa daityeṃdro vijigye sakalānsurān .. 33 ..
4.84.d: यत्र तप्त्वा स दैत्येंद्रो विजिग्ये सकलान्सुरान् .. 33 ..
4.84.m: Where, having performed tapas, that lord of Daityas conquered all the gods.
Even today, one who attends upon that tīrtha is not overcome by enemies,

4.84.s: na pātakairmahadbhiśca prārthitaṃ ca phalaṃ labhet .. 34 ..
4.84.d: न पातकैर्महद्भिश्च प्रार्थितं च फलं लभेत् .. 34 ..
4.84.m: nor by great sins, and he obtains his desired reward.
Near it is the Bāṇatīrtha, which bestowed a thousand arms [upon Bāṇa].

4.84.s: tatra snāto naro bhaktiṃ prāpnuyācchāṃbhavīṃ sthirām .. 35 ..
4.84.d: तत्र स्नातो नरो भक्तिं प्राप्नुयाच्छांभवीं स्थिराम् .. 35 ..
4.84.m: Having bathed there, a man attains steadfast devotion to Śambhu.
In front of it is an excellent tīrtha named Gopratāreśvara,
where even a sonless man, having bathed, crosses the Vaitaraṇī river with ease.
To its south is the tīrtha called Hiraṇyagarbha, which removes all sins;

4.84.s: tatra snāto hiraṇyena mucyate na kadācana ..37..
4.84.d: तत्र स्नातो हिरण्येन मुच्यते न कदाचन ..37..
4.84.m: having bathed there, he is never separated from gold.
Then there is Praṇavatīrtha, the highest of all excellent tīrthas;
a man becomes liberated while living merely by bathing there.
Then there is Piśaṅgilā tīrtha, which removes sin even by darśana.
O sage, Agastya, that is indeed my abode, which grants supreme perfections.

4.84.s: snātvā piśaṃgilā tīrthe dattvā dānaṃ ca kiṃcana ..
4.84.d: स्नात्वा पिशंगिला तीर्थे दत्त्वा दानं च किंचन ..
4.84.m: Having bathed in Piśaṅgilā tīrtha and given any gift,
why should he grieve over committed sin, even if he dies elsewhere?

4.84.s: yo vai piśaṃgilā tīrthe snātvā māmarcayiṣyati ..
4.84.d: यो वै पिशंगिला तीर्थे स्नात्वा मामर्चयिष्यति ..
4.84.m: Whoever, having bathed in Piśaṅgilā tīrtha, worships me,

4.84.s: bhaviṣyati sa me mittraṃ mitratejaḥ samaprabham .. 41 ..
4.84.d: भविष्यति स मे मित्त्रं मित्रतेजः समप्रभम् .. 41 ..
4.84.m: shall become my friend, endowed with splendor equal to the light of the sun.
Then there is the abundant tīrtha called Pilipilā,
cleansed by the sight of the gods, which destroys the impurities of the mind.
By performing the śrāddha and other rites there, and by offering satisfaction to the poor and helpless,
a man attains immense and exceedingly steadfast prosperity.
Then there is Nāgeśvara tīrtha, which cleanses away great sins;
the destruction of all sins occurs simply by plunging into that tīrtha.
To its south is an excellent, greatly meritorious [tīrtha] named Karṇāditya,
where a mortal, having bathed, attains solar splendor.
Then there is Bhairavatīrtha, which destroys heaps of great sins,
causes the four aims of life to rise, and removes all obstacles.
Having bathed there on a Tuesday falling on an aṣṭamī, a man should satisfy the ancestors;

4.84.s: dṛṣṭvā ca bhairavaṃ kālaṃ kaliṃ kālaṃ ca saṃjayet .. 47 ..
4.84.d: दृष्ट्वा च भैरवं कालं कलिं कालं च संजयेत् .. 47 ..
4.84.m: and having beheld Kāla Bhairava, he conquers Kali and Death.
Before the Bhairava tīrtha is the tīrtha named Kharvanṛsiṃha;

4.84.s: tatra snātasya vai puṃsaḥ kutoghajanitaṃ bhayam .. 48 ..
4.84.d: तत्र स्नातस्य वै पुंसः कुतोघजनितं भयम् .. 48 ..
4.84.m: for a man who has bathed there, whence could there be any fear born of sin?
To its south is the exceedingly pure tīrtha of the sage Mṛkaṇḍu;
by bathing there, mortals never suffer an untimely death.
Then there is the tīrtha called Pañcanada, resorted to by all tīrthas,

4.84.s: tīrthaṃ yatra naraḥ snātvā na saṃsārī punarbhavet .. 4.2.84.50 ..
4.84.d: तीर्थं यत्र नरः स्नात्वा न संसारी पुनर्भवेत् .. 4.2.84.50 ..
4.84.m: having bathed wherein a man is never again subject to transmigration.
Whatever tīrthas exist everywhere within the womb of the cosmic egg,
they all come there in the month of Kārttika to remove their own masses of sin.
All those foremost tīrthas always dwell there
for three days starting from the tenth [tithi], for the sake of their own purification.
All tīrthas are abundant at every step within Kāśī,
yet nowhere is the greatness of Pañcanada equaled by any.
Even a single day of Kārttika spent fruitfully there
through recitation, oblations, worship, and gifts makes people truly accomplished.
Even if all tīrthas were weighed simultaneously,
they would not attain equality even with a fraction of Pañcanadā.

4.84.s: snātvā pāṃcanade tīrthe dṛṣṭvā vai biṃdumādhavam ..
4.84.d: स्नात्वा पांचनदे तीर्थे दृष्ट्वा वै बिंदुमाधवम् ..
4.84.m: Having bathed in the Pañcanada tīrtha and beheld Bindumādhava,
the wise person is never again born in the courtyard of a mother's womb.
Then there is the tīrtha Jñānahrada, which removes dullness even of the inert;

4.84.s: tatra snāto naro jātu jñānabhraṃśaṃ na cāpnuyāt .. 57 ..
4.84.d: तत्र स्नातो नरो जातु ज्ञानभ्रंशं न चाप्नुयात् .. 57 ..
4.84.m: having bathed there, a man never suffers a lapse of knowledge.

4.84.s: tatra jñānahrade snātvā dṛṣṭvā jñāneśvaraṃ naraḥ ..
4.84.d: तत्र ज्ञानह्रदे स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा ज्ञानेश्वरं नरः ..
4.84.m: Having bathed there in Jñānahrada and beheld Jñāneśvara,

4.84.s: jñānaṃ tadadhigacchedvai yena no bādhyate punaḥ .. 58 ..
4.84.d: ज्ञानं तदधिगच्छेद्वै येन नो बाध्यते पुनः .. 58 ..
4.84.m: a man attains that knowledge by which he is never afflicted again.
Then there is Maṅgalatīrtha, which destroys all inauspiciousness;
having taken a bath there, one becomes a vessel of auspiciousness.
Inauspicious things perish and auspicious things arise
for one who bathes in Maṅgalatīrtha and bows to Maṅgala.
In front of it is the impurity-destroying tīrtha of Mayūkhamālin;
having bathed there and beheld Gabhastīśa, one becomes stainless.
Right there is Makhatīrtha, near Makheśvara;
having bathed there, an excellent man obtains the merit born of Vedic sacrifices.
Beside it is Bindutīrtha, the cause of supreme knowledge,
Having performed the ancestral rite and other rites there, one obtains the highest merit.
And the sacred ford of the sage Pippalāda is situated to its south.
Having bathed there on a Saturday and having indeed beheld Pippaleśvara,

4.84.s: pippalaṃ tatra sevitvā aśvattha iti maṃtrataḥ ..
4.84.d: पिप्पलं तत्र सेवित्वा अश्वत्थ इति मंत्रतः ..
4.84.m: and having honoured the peepal tree there with the mantra 'aśvattha',

4.84.s: śanipīḍāṃ na labhate duḥsvapnaṃ cāpi nāśayet .. 65 ..
4.84.d: शनिपीडां न लभते दुःस्वप्नं चापि नाशयेत् .. 65 ..
4.84.m: one does not suffer affliction from Saturn, and it also destroys bad dreams.
Then there is the exceedingly purifying sacred ford named Tāmravarāha,
where by bathing and giving gifts one will not sink into the ocean of sin.
In front of it is Kālagaṅgā, which destroys the blemishes of the Kali age.
Having bathed in it, a wise person becomes instantly free from sin.
The great sacred ford Indradyumna lies in front of Indradyumneśvara.
Having performed the water rite there, one attains the world of Indra.
Then there is the Rāmatīrtha, in front of Vīrarāmeśvara.
Merely by bathing in that sacred ford, one attains the world of Viṣṇu.
Then there is the Aikṣvākava sacred ford, which destroys all floods of sin.
By bathing there, the best of men becomes purified in soul.
At its edge is the Marutta sacred ford, in the presence of Marutteśvara.
Having bathed there and worshipped that Lord, one attains great sovereignty.
Then there is the Maitrāvaruṇa sacred ford, which destroys sins.
By offering a rice-ball there, one becomes dear to the ancestors.
Then there is the great, pure Agnitīrtha in front of Agnīśa.
One attains the world of Agni from immersing oneself in that sacred ford.
Right there is the Aṅgāratīrtha, in the presence of Aṅgāreśvara.
Having bathed there on the fourth lunar day of Tuesday, one surely reaches sinlessness.
Then indeed is the Kalitīrtha, in the presence of Kalaśeśvara.
Having bathed and worshipped that liṅga, they do not fear the Kali age.
And right there is Candratīrtha, near Candreśvara.
Having bathed there and worshipped Candreśa, one attains the world of the Moon.
In front of it is the Vīratīrtha, near Vīreśvara,
which was described before you earlier, supreme and the best of sacred fords.
Then there is the Vighneśatīrtha, which removes all obstacles.
One who bathes there at any time is never overcome by obstacles.
Then there is the unexcelled sacred ford of the royal sage Hariścandra,

4.84.s: yatra snāto naro jātu na satyāccayavate kacit .. 79 ..
4.84.d: यत्र स्नातो नरो जातु न सत्याच्चयवते कचित् .. 79 ..
4.84.m: having bathed in which a person never falls away from truth at any time.
Whatever good is acquired at the sacred ford of Hariścandra,

4.84.s: tadakṣayaphalaṃ vīra iha loke paratra ca .. 4.2.84.80 ..
4.84.d: तदक्षयफलं वीर इह लोके परत्र च .. 4.2.84.80 ..
4.84.m: its fruit is imperishable, O hero, both in this world and the next.
Then there is the Parvatatīrtha, near Parvateśa.
One who bathes [there] on holy days or non-holy days obtains the fruit of all holy days.
The Kambalāśvatara sacred ford there removes all poisons.
A mortal who bathes there becomes skilled in the science of music.
Then there is the sacred ford of Sarasvatī, which bestows all knowledge.
The ancestors stay there together with divine seers and men.
Right there is the Umātīrtha, endowed with all power.
Merely by bathing [there], one will certainly attain the world of Umā.
Then there is the sacred ford renowned throughout the three worlds, capable of delivering the three worlds,
most excellent, O hero, whose name is Maṇikarṇikā.
The Cakrapuṣkariṇī sacred ford was made there in the beginning by Viṣṇu.
Merely from the sound of its name in the ear, one is freed from all sins.
The dwellers of heaven recite 'Maṇikarṇikā' at the three junctions of the day,
for uttering its name leads to the highest good for men.

4.84.s: yaiḥ śrutā yaiḥ smṛtā vīra yairdṛṣṭā maṇikarṇikā ..
4.84.d: यैः श्रुता यैः स्मृता वीर यैर्दृष्टा मणिकर्णिका ..
4.84.m: Those by whom Maṇikarṇikā has been heard, remembered, or seen, O hero,

4.84.s: ta eva kṛtino loke kṛtakṛtyāsta eva hi .. 88 ..
4.84.d: त एव कृतिनो लोके कृतकृत्यास्त एव हि .. 88 ..
4.84.m: they alone are fortunate in the world; they alone have accomplished their goal.
Whatever men here in the three worlds recite 'Maṇikarṇikā',
those performers of meritorious deeds, O hero, I recite at the three periods of the day.
Sacrifices with hundreds of thousands of sacrificial gifts have been offered by him,
by whom 'Maṇikarṇikā', the five-syllabled great knowledge, has been uttered.
Great gifts have indeed been given by that performer of meritorious deeds,
by whom, having reached Maṇikarṇikā, I have been worshipped, O hero.
By him by whom the paternal great-grandfathers were gratified with the waters of Maṇikarṇī,
ancestral rites were given at Gayā with honey and milk-rice.
By him by whom the water of Maṇikarṇī has been drunk with a pure mind,
What need has he of those draughts of Soma which are characterised by return [to worldly rebirth]?
They have bathed in all sacred fords, abundantly on the great auspicious occasions,
and likewise with all concluding ceremonial baths, by whom Maṇikarṇikā has been bathed in.

4.84.s: taiḥ surāḥ pūjitāḥ sarve brahmaviṣṇumukhā makhaiḥ ..
4.84.d: तैः सुराः पूजिताः सर्वे ब्रह्मविष्णुमुखा मखैः ..
4.84.m: By them all gods, headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, have been worshipped with sacrifices;
by them Maṇikarṇikā has been worshipped with golden flowers and jewels.

4.84.s: ahaṃ tenomayā sārdhaṃ dīkṣāṃ saṃprāpya śāṃbhavīm ..
4.84.d: अहं तेनोमया सार्धं दीक्षां संप्राप्य शांभवीम् ..
4.84.m: Together with Umā, having received the Śaiva initiation,
I am worshipped daily by him by whom [Maṇi]karṇikā is worshipped.
Austerities have been performed by him for a long time with withered leaves and the like,
by whom glorious Maṇikarṇikā has been attended upon with faith.

4.84.s: dattvā dānāni bhūrīṇi makhāniṣṭvā tu bhūriśaḥ ..
4.84.d: दत्त्वा दानानि भूरीणि मखानिष्ट्वा तु भूरिशः ..
4.84.m: Having given abundant gifts and having performed sacrifices abundantly,
having performed austerities for a long time in forests, [instead of falling] from heavenly sovereignty to earth again,
here upon the broad surface of the earth, within the five-krośa circuit, the charming [ford]—
they who have resorted to this Maṇikarṇī have departed, never to return.

4.84.s: dānānāṃ ca vratānāṃ ca kratūnāṃ tapasāmapi ..
4.84.d: दानानां च व्रतानां च क्रतूनां तपसामपि ..
4.84.m: Of gifts, vows, sacrifices, and also of austerities,
I consider this alone to be the fruit: that Maṇikarṇikā is attained.
This glorious Maṇikarṇikā is the fortune of liberation in person;
indeed, I too do not clearly know its majesty fully.
To the south of Maṇikarṇī is the supreme Pāśupata ford;
then the sacred ford named Rudravāsa, and beyond that Viśvatīrtha;
then the delightful Muktitīrtha, and then the supreme Avimukta;

4.84.s: tīrthaṃ ca tārakaṃ skāṃdaṃ ḍhuṃḍhestīrthaṃ tatopi ca .. 3 ..
4.84.d: तीर्थं च तारकं स्कांदं ढुंढेस्तीर्थं ततोपि च .. 3 ..
4.84.m: and the Tāraka ford, the Skānda, and then also the ford of Ḍhuṇḍhi;
then Bhavāneya, then Aiśāna, and then the supreme Jñānatīrtha;
Nanditīrtha, Viṣṇutīrtha, and then the Paitāmaha ford;
this Nābhitīrtha, and beyond that Brahmanāla;
then the Bhāgīratha ford, which was related to you before.
In the heavenly river flowing northward near Kāśī,
there are many holy sacred fords; they have been spoken of by me in brief.
Even among them, the Pañcatīrthī is exceedingly superior, O prince,

4.84.s: yasyāṃ stātvā naro bhūyo garbhavāsaṃ na saṃsmaret .. 7 ..
4.84.d: यस्यां स्तात्वा नरो भूयो गर्भवासं न संस्मरेत् .. 7 ..
4.84.m: having bathed in which, a man never again remembers dwelling in a womb.
First is the confluence with the Asi, supreme among sacred fords;
then the one named Daśāśvamedha, resorted to by all sacred fords;

By it the ground of the sacrificial pavilion was instantly made uneven.
An unexpected lightning strike occurred, shaking the earth.
Meteors fell from the sky, and piśācas began to dance.
Cruel vultures wheeled in circles high above in the sky.
Beneath the sun, female jackals howled inauspiciously.
Clouds released a heavy shower of blood-drops there.

The great sacrificial substance to be offered was defiled by jackals and dogs;

In an instant, that sacrificial enclosure became like a cremation ground.
Whatever stood in any place remained fixed right there;
